comments.text: First, let me say that when you finish nursing school, you graduate then you get to take your NCLEX. That is a state exam  to practice nursing. If you pass, you receive a license number and license. I received mine in 1999. I worked med-surg night shift for awhile. I had 13 patients as a new RN. It was crazy and dangerous. Later, I left hospital nursing but still have my license and keep it up. Back in 1999, I started at $17.82 an hour. That was shift differential pay here in Texas. In Texas, they still don't pay nurses enough for the responsibility that we have. We need to educate society about what nursing school is like and your first job. Maybe someone can make a documentary on it. Nurses are greatly misunderstood and under rated. We carry out a lot of responsibility that the public doesn't even know about. I guess they think we just sit at computers all the time. Something needs to be done to change societies view and value on nurses!
